title: Fine-Grained Authorization
summary: Fine-grained authorization answers 'can Anne view this document?' when the answer depends on relationships: she is in a group that is an editor of the folder that contains the document. Inspired by Google's Zanzibar, the system stores relationship tuples, uses a schema to define how relations imply each other, and evaluates checks by walking that graph quickly and consistently, so a user removed from a document cannot still see it a second later.

walkthrough.title: Share a document
walkthrough.text: Bob shares the readme with the eng team. The app writes a tuple: doc:readme#viewer@group:eng#member.

walkthrough.title: Store with a consistency token
walkthrough.text: The tuple is committed with a timestamp, and a consistency token ('zookie') is returned. The app stores it alongside the document's content version.

walkthrough.title: Check access
walkthrough.text: Anne opens the document. The app calls check(doc:readme, view, user:anne) and passes the document's zookie.

walkthrough.title: Expand with the schema
walkthrough.text: The schema says view = viewer + editor + parent folder's viewers. The service evaluates these rewrite rules, fanning out subproblems in parallel.

walkthrough.title: Read at a snapshot
walkthrough.text: Tuples are read at a snapshot at least as new as the zookie. That solves the 'new enemy' problem: someone removed before the content change cannot see the new content.

walkthrough.title: Use precomputed group membership
walkthrough.text: Deeply nested groups (team ⊂ org ⊂ company) are flattened into a precomputed index, so membership checks are fast set lookups instead of long graph walks.

walkthrough.title: Stream changes downstream
walkthrough.text: A Watch API streams tuple changes so search indexes and caches can filter results by permission without calling check for every item.

data.label: Application
responsibilities: Writes relationships whenever sharing or membership changes.
Checks permission before every protected read or action.

failureModes.scenario: App checks its own copy of permissions
failureModes.mitigation: One central authorization service for all products.

failureModes.scenario: Forgot to check on a new endpoint
failureModes.mitigation: Deny-by-default middleware and tests for every route.

data.label: Authorization Service

output.name: Decision
output.type: Allowed / denied in ~10 ms at p95

responsibilities: Evaluates checks by walking the relationship graph.
Honours consistency tokens on every read.

failureModes.mitigation: Depth limits, flattened group indexes, parallel fan-out.

failureModes.impact: Every product fails closed: nobody can open anything.
failureModes.mitigation: Multi-region replicas; aggressive caching for zookie-free checks.

data.label: Namespace Schema

input.name: Definition
input.type: definition doc { relation parent: folder; relation viewer: user | group#member }

responsibilities: Defines object types, relations, and how permissions derive from them.
Keeps policy logic out of application code.
Is validated and tested before deployment.

failureModes.impact: Users suddenly see data they should not.
failureModes.mitigation: Schema tests with expected allow/deny assertions in CI.

failureModes.scenario: Removing a relation still in use
failureModes.mitigation: Migration checks that no tuples use a relation before it is removed.

data.label: Relationship Tuple Store

output.name: Read
output.type: Tuples for an object at snapshot T

responsibilities: Stores billions of relationship tuples durably.
Serves reads at a chosen snapshot timestamp.
Keeps a changelog of every write.

failureModes.scenario: Reading a stale replica without a token
failureModes.impact: A removed user briefly keeps access (new enemy problem).
failureModes.mitigation: Read at a snapshot no older than the content's zookie.
Caching and the flattened membership index.

data.label: Watch Consumers
responsibilities: Keeps search and listing indexes permission-aware.
Feeds audit trails of access changes.

failureModes.impact: Search shows items a user just lost access to.
failureModes.mitigation: Post-filter search results with check; alert on lag.
Resume from a stored revision; periodic full rebuilds.

data.label: Group Membership Index
responsibilities: Turns deep recursive checks into set intersections.

failureModes.impact: Slower checks until it is rebuilt.
failureModes.mitigation: Fall back to graph walking; rebuild from the tuple store.
Special-case public or company-wide grants as wildcards.
